media.alt: Common heart diseases in newborns, infants and children

content.text: "Five to eight out of a thousand births have congenital heart disease. Some of these defects are minor whereas majority would manifest with such severity, as to need urgent medical attention. Some children who have a heart defect from birth appear cyanosed (blue) at a variable time interval after birth. The cyanosis is more evident when the baby cries. A baby who is blue at birth may have a serious heart disease and may need urgent examination by a doctor and evaluation by a paediatric cardiologist. Such babies also usually need urgent cardiac surgery", informed Dr Mehnaz Atiq, Consultant Paediatric Cardiologist and Assistant Professor of Paediatrics, The Aga Khan University Hospital. She was giving a presentation on "Common Heart Diseases in Newborns, Infants and Children" at 'Signs, Symptoms and Care', monthly health awareness program, held on November 27, 1999.

Dr Mehnaz added, "Infants who are not blue may have a disease that causes recurrent pneumonia or congestive cardiac failure. Such babies can be managed on drug therapy but require repeated cardiovascular examination for timely cardiac surgery."

Dr Mehnaz concluded by saying that there are other cardiac diseases which an infant or a child can acquire later in life, most importantly, the rheumatic heart disease. This disease afflicts children above five years of age and stems from an initial sore throat caused by a specific bacterial agent called "Group A, B-hemolytic streptococcus". Rheumatic fever manifests most of the time with either joint pains or cardiac disease. Patients with this disease require long term preventive treatment with Penicillin."
